clue.text: Comic friend of Ollie attending party in Belfast

indicators.note: attending means being beside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner
the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A comedian who partners Oliver Hardy goes to a political party in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were Stan and Ollie; the DUP is a Northern Irish party, based in Belfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up is a solo comedian performing live, so a comic in noun form.

clue.text: Food and drink for entertaining politician leading old city

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the drink's letters go round the rest

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: leading means coming in front, so the politician goes before the city

parts.note: MP is Member of Parliament
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Refreshments laid on to host a politician in charge of an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura is a Japanese dish of battered, deep-fried fish or vegetables, an example of food.

clue.text: End troubled about a king in the altogether

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the rest
troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the word end are rearranged

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king meets a troubled ending while undressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges END into NED, which goes 'about' AK.
explanation.definitionFit: In the altogether is a British idiom for wearing no clothes at all, i.e. nude.

clue.text: Offence caused by display of buttocks, bishop coming down with anger

indicators.note: in a down clue coming down means the bishop's letter drops lower, to the end

parts.note: bum is British slang for the buttocks
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rage is fierce anger

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence at a bishop baring his bottom in a fit of temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming down' moves the B of BUM to the bottom, giving UMB.
explanation.definitionFit: To take umbrage is to take offence, so the word names a feeling of resentment.

clue.text: In dispute, heard report of expulsion

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is taken as it would sound when spoken

parts.note: a matter at issue is one in dispute

explanation.surface: Someone in a quarrel hears news that a person has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expulsion' is not an eviction but the blast of air in a sneeze; 'report' is its noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the British written sound of a sneeze, the noise made as air is expelled.

clue.text: Short journey with poem in the Tube

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a journey
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A brief trip with some poetry on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Tube' suggests the London Underground; here it is a valve.
explanation.definitionFit: A triode is a thermionic valve with three electrodes, called a vacuum tube in American usage.

clue.text: Friends gathering around wife — after end of troubles they cry

indicators.note: after means the rest follows that letter
end of picks the final letter of the word troubles
gathering around means enclosing, so the Friends' letters go round the wife

parts.note: Quakers are members of the Religious Society of Friends

explanation.surface: Friends huddle round a wife who weeps when her troubles end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friends' with a capital is the Quaker Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Squawkers are those who make harsh screeching calls, like noisy birds crying out.

clue.text: Abuse of cocaine widespread?

indicators.note: abuse means maltreatment, so the letters of the drug are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Is cocaine misuse rife?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'widespread' is a loose, playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceanic means vast or immense, like the sea, so the word suggests something spread far and wide.

clue.text: Vehicle on notable run aiming to be eco-friendly

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: aiming means directing, so these letters are pointed into a new order

explanation.surface: A car on a famous drive tries to be green.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon neutral describes activity whose emissions are balanced by offsets, a key environmental goal.

clue.text: City's form is OK, every now and then

indicators.note: every now and then means occasionally, so only every other letter of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A city's condition is fine, from time to time.
explanation.definitionFit: Omsk is a large Siberian city in Russia on the Irtysh river.

clue.text: One union in debates spouting pious words

indicators.note: in means placed inside the rearranged letters
spouting means gushing out wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A trade union speaker spouts sanctimonious phrases during debates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spouting' signals the rearrangement; 'One union' looks like a single body but is two abbreviations, I and TU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatitudes are Christ's blessings in the Sermon on the Mount, sayings of religious devotion.

clue.text: Container for ale, mostly dull and plain

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for beer or wine

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: drab means dull

explanation.surface: A beer cask that is largely dull and unadorned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like an adjective beside 'dull' but is a noun: a flat expanse.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless Arctic flatland, a kind of frozen plain.

clue.text: Sprinkling part of garden on eastern side

parts.note: a flower bed is part of a garden
a wing is a side of a building or a team

explanation.surface: Watering a flower bed on the east side of the grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedewing means wetting with drops as if with dew, a light sprinkling of moisture.

clue.text: Like a prophet travelling once around Rome, say

indicators.note: around means the travelling word goes round the other piece

parts.note: faring is an old word for travelling
the Holy See is the bishopric of Rome, an example of a see

explanation.surface: A prophet-like figure once journeyed around Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome, say' suggests a city; it is a See, a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-seeing means able to foresee the future, the gift a prophet is credited with.

clue.text: Strong man turning up, politician dancing and jumping

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: Atlas is the Titan who held up the sky, a byword for strength
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A muscleman arrives while a politician capers and leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltatory means relating to leaping or to dance, from the Latin for leaping.

clue.text: Second-rate 'Strictly' participant entertaining one and all — such may offer fun at Blackpool?

definitions.text: such may offer fun at Blackpool?

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the outer letters hold the rest

parts.note: B is a second-class mark
Ed Balls, the former Labour minister, danced on Strictly Come Dancing
each means every one, so one and all

explanation.surface: A mediocre ballroom contestant hosts everyone for seaside fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly Come Dancing is a BBC ballroom show; Blackpool is a British seaside resort where it holds a famous episode.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflatable beach balls are toys for playing on the sand at a seaside resort.

clue.text: See 16
Tricky navigation — a time one must leave city with a bridge

indicators.note: tricky means awkward, so the letters are muddled
must leave means these letters are taken out of the mixed-up pool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Steering is hard, and a traveller must depart a bridged city on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix NAVIGATION and take out A, T and I, which 'must leave'.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon in southern France is known for its medieval bridge, the Pont Saint-Bénézet.

clue.text: Is brevity so different? Yes!

indicators.note: different means changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: is wordiness the opposite of being brief? Indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as the very opposite of brevity.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbosity is excessive wordiness, the direct opposite of keeping things short.

clue.text: African people go off into depot

indicators.note: into means placed inside the other piece

parts.note: a base is a depot
to rot is to go off, decay

explanation.surface: Some Africans head off to a depot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barotse, or Lozi, are a Bantu people of western Zambia.

clue.text: Volunteers having to hang around a large area once

indicators.note: around means the lingering word wraps round the volunteers

parts.note: to tarry is to hang about, linger
the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Volunteers have to wait around a vast region of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartary was the historical European name for the vast lands of Central Asia.

clue.text: Boaster's idle talk, something to fool you?

parts.note: gas is empty chatter
a con is a trick

explanation.surface: A braggart's chatter is a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascon, from the Gascony people's reputation, means a braggart.

clue.text: Performance by a Kentish rebel not half showing a lot of power

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance

indicators.note: not half means half the letters are dropped

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 from Kent

explanation.surface: A show by a rebel from Kent, not fully displaying great power.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the 1381 Peasants' Revolt, starting in Kent, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigawatt is a billion watts, a vast quantity of electrical energy output.

clue.text: See paper suffering setback — get angry about it

indicators.note: about it means the angry word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to go red is to get angry, so red is angry

indicators.note: suffering setback means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: rag is slang for a poor newspaper

explanation.surface: Look at a newspaper in decline and fume about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at or consider, a synonym of see as a verb.

clue.text: Paid pounds for something at auction

parts.note: gave means handed over money
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Money handed over for a lot at a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavel is the auctioneer's hammer, struck to close each sale.

clue.text: Casual home worker, collecting very little money, starts to complain intensely

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so these letters surround the rest

parts.note: in means at home
an ant is a worker
a sou is a French coin of tiny value

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A laid-back home worker, earning pennies, begins to grumble hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home worker' reads as one person working from home, but it is two pieces that together go round the money and the starts; a sou was an old French coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Insouciant means cheerfully unconcerned, a carefree, casual attitude.

clue.text: Bottle of essential medicament finally disposed of

indicators.note: disposed of means thrown away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: vital means essential

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word medicament

explanation.surface: A bottle of vital medicine, eventually thrown away.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass container, a little bottle for medicine.

clue.text: Wanting to be like opponents at table competing

parts.note: East and North are opposing partnerships at the bridge table
vying means competing

explanation.surface: Wishing to emulate rivals at cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Envying is coveting what another has, wishing oneself in their place.

clue.text: Recordings of songs introduced by agent

indicators.note: introduced by means the agent comes first

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
lays are songs or ballads

explanation.surface: Song recordings presented by a sales agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Replays are recordings played back, such as repeated footage of a match.
